brief: August US nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000, with private payrolls up 127,000, against a 55,000 consensus. Positive revisions added 55,000 jobs to prior months, lifting the three-month private-employment average to 75,000, above the 0-60,000 breakeven range for a stable unemployment rate. Unemployment held at 4.1% as job creation was offset by higher labor force participation. Combined with a 3.7% year-on-year July PCE inflation print, hawkish Fed Chair Kevin Warsh comments at Jackson Hole, and worsening supplier-delivery times in recent ISM and PMI surveys, this pushed market-implied odds of a September Fed hike from about 50% to 60%. UBS changed its base case from rates unchanged through 2026 to two 25 basis-point hikes, in September and December, taking the fed funds target range to 4.00-4.25%, and raised its yield forecasts to 4.25% for 2-year and 4.5% for 10-year Treasuries by June 2027. A second hike could be postponed if inflation readings through October average below 2% annualized. Because UBS reads the hikes as a response to economic strength rather than inflation problems, its constructive equity view, favoring AI, Power and resources, and Longevity, is unchanged. It no longer recommends locking in short- to medium-duration bond yields as a cash alternative.
